A positive answer would make every countable group MF, because the reduced group C*-algebra is separable and stably finite; Lubotzky-Oppenheim and, separately, Thom noted this... NEW theorem (landed by s-intro): the printed sentence is itself conditional ("would make"), so a conditional theorem (every separable stably finite C*-algebra is MF => every countable group is MF, via reducedGroupCStar_separable_stablyFinite + isCDEOperatorMF_of_hasMFEmbedding_reducedGroupCStar) is the faithful formalization. The MF problem itself was answered negatively in 2020: the failure of the Connes embedding problem [MIPRE] yields a II_1 factor that embeds in no norm ultraproduct of matrix algebras, hence a separable stably finite C*-algebra that is not MF [Prop 6.1, Remark 6.2]{GoldbringHart}. printedNegativeConnesEmbeddingSentence proves the mathematical conclusion (a separable stably finite non-MF C*-algebra exists, exhibited by the paper's own reduced group algebra) unconditionally; the historical MIPRE/Connes-embedding route is provenance/attribution, not re-derived.
